caveats: Burgess bias = overlap fraction x |r_g| is an approximation (Burgess 2016); the 70%-of-BMD denominator is the fraction of the EXPOSURE sample shared, appropriate for asking whether the two-sample assumption holds for the BMD instrument -> fracture path; the 8.4%-of-fracture denominator is the fraction of the OUTCOME sample shared. Both describe the SAME 22,330 people.

LABEL ERROR CORRECTED: manuscript S14 and docs/148 P1-2 previously wrote 'up to ~12% on the 70%-of-BMD basis'. But 70% x |r_g|=0.4868 = 34.1%, NOT 12%. The ~12% figure actually corresponds to the symmetric geometric-mean overlap sqrt(0.701 x 0.084)=24.3% x |r_g| ~ 11.8-12.4% (code/121 used overlap~0.23, consistent with this). The three denominators (8.4% / geometric-mean 24.3% / 70%) now each carry their correctly-derived bias (4.1% / ~12% / 34%). The literal Burgess formula is olsbias x overlap.prop x (1/F); the manuscript's overlap x r_g omits the 1/F attenuation and is a conservative upper bound, so even the 34% is a worst-case ceiling, not an expected bias.

MRlap re-clumps to 48 (total) / 34 (femur-neck) instruments, not the primary 31/25, and reports effects on its own exposure scale; its raw corrected beta is therefore NOT the Table 2 corrected OR. We transfer the scale-free ratio corrected/observed onto the Table 2 IVW beta, which assumes the RELATIVE overlap displacement is approximately instrument-set invariant.
This transfer is a sensitivity analysis, not a substitute point estimate; the primary Table 2 OR (1.40/1.42) remains the reported value.
